- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent mean), model often overshoots — cap next 3–5 days’ forecast at +5% above peak.
- If sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive, model overreacts — dampen forecast rise by 10–15% in first 2–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is consistently 5–8% above true outcome over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 2–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility — smooth forecast curve by reducing standard deviation by 15–20% relative to historical volatility.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to overpredict — adjust downward by 2–5% if true outcome is below 75% of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes, model underreacts — increase forecast by 3–5% to compensate for lagged sentiment effect.
